data.long_meaning: Hebrew: 'Esdras' (חזרה) means 'God has helped' or 'God's help'. In the Bible, Esdras was a priest, scribe, and leader who helped the Israelites return to Jerusalem and rebuild the Temple. The name Esdras carries the meaning “God's help” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Esdras usually hope their child will grow to embody god's help and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: Esdras is a significant figure in Jewish and Christian history, particularly celebrated in the books of the Old Testament, Ezra and Nehemiah. He led a group of exiles back to Jerusalem in 458 BC and played a crucial role in the rebuilding of the Second Temple. His name, 'Esdras', denotes his role as a leader and a helper, demonstrating his contribution to the restoration and preservation of Jewish culture.

The name 'Esdras' carries a reminder of hope and the power of faith to initiate change and restore what has been lost.
